summary: Frontend-only styling/contrast audit of the CloudIVR auth pages and in-app pages, in light and dark themes, at 1920 and 390 widths. I wrote an automated WCAG contrast scanner (/app/tests/contrast_scan.js). It walks every visible text node and input placeholder, blends semi-transparent backgrounds and opacity, and flags anything under 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text). I ran it on login/signup/forgot, the 18 app pages listed below, all 14 number-detail tabs, the command palette, the language dropdown, What's new, the support chat, the add-contact modal, the wallet top-up (deposit address), the sonner toast, and on mobile overview, the More menu and 4 pages. Login worked for Alice (UI). The theme toggle (topbar-theme-button) switches between dark and light and saves the choice in localStorage civr.theme. app-sidebar is rgb(19,23,28) in both themes. auth-side-panel is #13171c with white text in both themes. Nothing scrolls sideways at 390. The landing page is still dark and fine. I found several real issues, mainly that the dialogs were near-black in light mode, and fixed them with small CSS mapping rules in theme-clean.css. A final full re-scan was clean except for the disabled 'Coming soon' card on the wallet page.

ui_bugs.component: Command palette, confirm dialog, Upgrade modal, What's new, contacts Modal, SupportChat panel, Text-to-voice 'Tell them it's a typed call' row
ui_bugs.issue: LIGHT theme: these use important (!) Tailwind classes !bg-[#111] / !bg-[#0f0f0f] / !bg-[#0e0e10], and theme-light.css had no mapping for them. The surfaces stayed near-black and the dark text on them was unreadable: the palette number row was invisible and the text-call label measured 1.07:1. FIXED in theme-clean.css (they now use var(--c-card), with !important, in both themes).

ui_bugs.component: Dashboard 'Quick actions' and the stat label
ui_bugs.issue: LIGHT: .civr-label.!text-[#a1a1aa] measured #a1a1aa on white, 2.56:1. FIXED with a light rule for !text-[#a1a1aa] (now #556070).

LIGHT: #1f6fd6 text on the accent-soft tint measured 4.39:1 on topbar-balance, the 'New' pills on the dashboard and wallet-preset-*. FIXED: light --c-accent-soft lowered to 0.05 and .civr-pill-on text set to #185bb3.

LIGHT, mobile top bar and auth mobile header: the inline #34d399 measured 1.92:1 on white. FIXED with a #059669 override for [data-testid=topbar-logo] and [data-testid=auth-mobile-logo-link]. The owner may prefer to make this change in Brand.js accent instead.
!text-[#fb7185] (delete/hang-up/logout buttons) and !text-[#fbbf24] (OrderStatus simulate) had no light mapping and were about 2.6:1 and 1.7:1 on white. FIXED: now #e11d48 and #b45309.
ui_bugs.selector: MobileNav mobile-logout-button, contacts delete, quick/Otp hangup, CallNote, buy/OrderStatus

ui_bugs.issue: placeholder:text-[#71717a] on #23272d measured 3.1:1. FIXED with a dark mapping (#8593a8).
#008a2e on #ecfdf3 measured 4.26:1. FIXED with --success-text #046c2a and --info-text on [data-sonner-toaster].

issues: Not fixed. The disabled card has opacity-70, so the 'Coming soon' badge measures 4.35:1 and the card description 3.59:1. This passes WCAG because disabled components are exempt; raise to opacity-80 if you want it more readable. Selectors: [data-testid=wallet-method-card], [data-testid=wallet-method-card-badge] (CardComingSoon in pages/buy/Checkout.js).
Not fixed. The '·' separator in [data-testid=number-sms-reach-chip] > span.opacity-70 measures 4.26:1. It is decorative only.

Not changed, owner decision. [data-testid=mobile-more-menu] is white in light mode while the desktop side menu is graphite in both themes. Readable, but it does not follow the 'graphite menu in both themes' choice.
Not changed. The VISA/AMEX/DISCOVER/Debit logo chips measure about 2.7–4.1:1. These are brand logos and are exempt.

action_items: Review the CSS rules I appended at the end of frontend/src/cloudivr/theme-clean.css (from the 'Important (!) dark utility classes' comment onward) and keep or adjust them.
Optional: for important (!) colour utilities added later, also add light and dark mappings. theme-light.css only maps the non-important classes.
Optional: make the mobile More menu graphite in light mode too, for consistency with the side menu.
Optional: the disabled 'Coming soon' card could use opacity-80.
critical_code_review_comments: Theme mapping depends on hand-maintained class-escape lists. Important utilities (!bg-[#111] etc.) slipped through; a grep check for '![a-z-]*\[#' would catch new ones.
Wordmark uses an inline style color (#34d399), so no theme can recolour it without !important. Make the accent theme-aware in Brand.js.

success_rate.frontend: about 97% after fixes (one exempt disabled-card item remains)
